drivers.connection: Sikh / Udasi families beside the North
drivers.reason: The Sikh / Udasi families occupy 14–16 beside the North. The uniform has an approved proposed destination in 18; 17 and 70 retain mounting checks for other large objects. Regional proximity does not imply a teacher relationship.

The four Buddhist source records move together to 25, in a separately labelled group alongside other eastern holdings. The combined recorded load is 4.4202 shares. Shared housing does not put the neighboring saints into a Buddhist lineage.

Dadu and the Girnar/Nath groups move into 58–61, facing the existing western island across the entrance-room aisle. The entire former 81 group, including the Brahma Kumaris, moves to 62. Their subgroups retain distinct labels.

drivers.connection: Samarth Ramdas at the Ram Bhakti boundary
drivers.reason: Samarth’s full immediate group moves to 80; the existing 80 continuation moves to 81. This puts his Rama devotion near the Mirabai/Ravidas/Ramanandi approach across the aisle. It is a thematic bridge, not a claim that Samarth was a Ramanandi disciple.

drivers.connection: The South continues around the entrance room
drivers.reason: Southern families remain together in 51–57 and move in intact groups to 63 and 65–68. Vitrine 64 holds the separate spade; 69 is potential southern expansion. Reuse of 68 depends on verified replacement housing for the large Sikh relics.

Ramanuja joins Ramana at57. Nityananda and his existing four-person display family move together from46 to57, connecting his substantial Kerala work with Ganeshpuri. Other independent families in46 remain together there.

tradeoffs: Published for curator review as a proposed arrangement. Recorded current locations and physical move confirmations are preserved.
The uniform relocation is approved as a proposal. Physical execution is not confirmed; other exploratory allocations remain for review.
17 and 70 are provisional Sikh mounting allowances, not confirmed free capacity.
The Buddhist display shares 25 with separately labelled eastern cohorts; this is not a new tradition or personal relationship.
Samarth Ramdas 80 and the Ramanandi story are a cross-aisle thematic connection, not a shared guru lineage.
Place the southern families here only after replacement housing for the large Sikh relics is verified in the 17/70 allowance.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Varkari devotion
visitorStoryRoute.people: Tukaram · Namdev and Janabai · Savata Mali · Dnyaneshwar
visitorStoryRoute.story: Meet the Varkari saints through their own local settings, held together by devotion to Vithoba. Keep close companions beside one another.
visitorStoryRoute.transition: The Nivrittinath connection leads into the Nath setting.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Nath and western communities
visitorStoryRoute.people: Nath traditions · Jalaram · smaller western city groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Varkari story opens into Nath practice and the western local communities. Smaller displays gather by city around intact families.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Shegaon and Pune
visitorStoryRoute.people: Gajanan Maharaj · T.L. Vaswani and J.P. Vaswani
visitorStoryRoute.story: Shegaon gives Gajanan’s family a clear home. Keep the Vaswani succession legible as its own Pune group.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Rajasthan and Girnar
visitorStoryRoute.people: Dadu Dayal · Girnar families · Brahma Kumaris
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the local Girnar groups together. Dadu and the Brahma Kumaris retain their own traditions and centres alongside the other western communities.

visitorStoryRoute.title: BAPS succession
visitorStoryRoute.people: The BAPS guru family
visitorStoryRoute.story: One case presents the immediate succession together, with room to read its relationships.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Datta families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Dattatreya · Narasimha Saraswati · Akkalkot family
visitorStoryRoute.story: Read the distinct Datta branches as related devotional families. The Solapur marker locates the broader Akkalkot region, not every saint’s residence.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Shirdi, Sakori and Meher Baba
visitorStoryRoute.people: Shirdi Sai Baba · Upasani and Godavari · Meher Baba’s formation circle
visitorStoryRoute.story: Personal connections hold this display together across several western centres. Keep each close pair visible within the larger circle.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Puducherry to Pune
visitorStoryRoute.people: The Mother · Dilip Kumar Roy · Indira Devi
visitorStoryRoute.story: Their shared spiritual history creates the South–West bridge. Preserve the three together across their different life centres.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Kerala
visitorStoryRoute.people: Shivaprabhakara and Kerala families
visitorStoryRoute.story: A Kerala setting gathers the regional families. Give the principal anchor the clearest position, with smaller local groups below.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Tamil devotional settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Pamban Swamigal · Tamil Shaiva and Chennai groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Let Chennai-related displays sit together while retaining Pamban’s wider Tamil life story. A city grouping complements the immediate families.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Sri Vaishnava settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Srirangam Jeeyars · Hatiram / Hathiram identity-held grouping
visitorStoryRoute.story: Srirangam temple and teaching groups form a distinct cluster. Keep the Tirupati story separate; preserve the existing Hatiram identity question.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Southern highlights
visitorStoryRoute.people: Ramanujacharya · Ramana Maharshi · Bhagavan Nityananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Three distinct spiritual settings share the prime endcap. Nityananda’s four-person family stays together; his Kerala work opens a connection back toward Ganeshpuri in the West.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Southern continuation
visitorStoryRoute.people: Southern companion groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Continue with the local southern cohorts. Retain labels where the available city clue is provisional.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Haridwar’s large relic
visitorStoryRoute.people: Hanuman Das of Haridwar
visitorStoryRoute.story: The separate full-height spade retains its special housing. Its physical requirements are an exception to the regional sequence.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Kadapa and Andhra families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Veerabrahmendra · Siddhaiah
visitorStoryRoute.story: The teacher and disciple provide the Andhra anchor, with their close family kept together.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Guntur and Ram Nam
visitorStoryRoute.people: Andhra avadhuta groups · Ragam Rama Pitchaiah Garu
visitorStoryRoute.story: Preserve the reviewed guru groups. Gather smaller Guntur-related displays by locality, keeping the Ram Nam story visible.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Karnataka
visitorStoryRoute.people: Siddharoodha · Hubli–Mugalkhod families
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the Karnataka families legible. The use of68 depends on the Sikh large-object provision;69 becomes potential space after the uniform move.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Punjab and the Sikh gurus
visitorStoryRoute.people: Guru Nanak and Sri Chand · Sikh guru families · uniform
visitorStoryRoute.story: Read the Sikh and Udasi groups together along the wall beside the North. Keep the full-height uniform and other large-item allowances with this neighbourhood.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Badrinath
visitorStoryRoute.people: Badrinarayana · Badrinath companion groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: A Himalayan pilgrimage setting gathers the Badrinath-related displays.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Uttarkashi and Rishikesh
visitorStoryRoute.people: Tapovan · Chinmayananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the teacher and disciple together. Nearby smaller displays gather around their meaningful Himalayan cities.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Rishikesh teaching family
visitorStoryRoute.people: Sivananda · Chidananda · Vishnudevananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: The immediate teaching family remains together across the places where its work spread.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Northern review holdings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Identity under review
visitorStoryRoute.story: These labelled holdings retain their identity questions while the curator reviews them.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Kumaon
visitorStoryRoute.people: Haidakhan Babaji · Neem Karoli Baba
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Kumaon setting leads toward Neem Karoli’s North–Vraj connection. The Nainital marker is a regional reference, not an exact ashram location.

visitorStoryRoute.title: The Kriya tree
visitorStoryRoute.people: Babaji · Lahiri · Sri Yukteswar · Yogananda · related disciples
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the clear Kriya tree together in5. Its Varanasi and Bengal lives make it a natural bridge between North and East.
visitorStoryRoute.transition: Mahendranath Gupta supplies the personal connection into the next display.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ramakrishna’s family
visitorStoryRoute.people: Ramakrishna · Vivekananda · Mahendranath Gupta · Lakshmi Mani
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Dakshineswar/Kolkata setting anchors this family. Place Mahendranath Gupta toward Kriya to make his encounter with Yogananda easy to see.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Anandamayi Ma
visitorStoryRoute.people: Anandamayi Ma and her immediate family
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the mobile family together across Bengal and Kankhal. These two map markers orient the wider story; they are not a complete life route.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Shakta and Jaiguru settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bamakhepa · Omkarnath · Parankush and Jaiguru
visitorStoryRoute.story: Distinct local settings sit beside intact teaching families. Jaiguru connects Bengal and Puri without being split between them.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Eastern and Buddhist settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Assam and Bengal groups · distinct Buddhist display
visitorStoryRoute.story: Give Assam, Bengal and the Buddhist display their own identities inside this shared allocation.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Puri and Odisha
visitorStoryRoute.people: Jagannath · Gosaiji · Yogmaya · Kuladananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Puri leads into Gosaiji’s immediate family at the Vraj-facing endcap. Keep Cuttack and Nemalo-related smaller cohorts legible as their own local settings.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Gaudiya teaching families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bhaktisiddhanta · Prabhupada · Jagadbandhu · Tinkodi–Murari · Radharaman Charan Das
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Gaudiya story crosses Bengal, Puri and Vraj. Keep each immediate branch together rather than treating the full tradition as a single household.

visitorStoryRoute.title: The Mirabai hinge
visitorStoryRoute.people: Mirabai · Chaitanya and early Gaudiyas · Ravidas · Vraj Ramanandis
visitorStoryRoute.story: Independently prominent saints carry the bridge across neighbouring displays. Their distinct settings remain visible as the story turns toward Ram devotion.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ram devotion and Kashi
visitorStoryRoute.people: Tulsidas and Hanuman · Kabir · Trailanga and Shankari
visitorStoryRoute.story: Rama devotion leads into Kashi. Keep the close pairs together; preserve the different meanings of traditional relationships and personal encounters.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ram devotion from the West
visitorStoryRoute.people: Samarth Ramdas
visitorStoryRoute.story: The western Ram-bhakti story meets the Ramanandi side of the hinge through shared devotion, while retaining its own lineage.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Vraj’s local traditions
visitorStoryRoute.people: Banke Bihari · Radha Raman · Surdas and Pushtimarg · modern Vraj groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Adjacent deity displays begin a local Vraj story. Continue through the different traditions and keep Devraha–Devra Hansa and other close families together.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Bhakti Marga and global contexts
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bhakti Marga families and global connections
visitorStoryRoute.story: These displays extend the museum’s Indian stories into the wider world.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Walking-stick displays
visitorStoryRoute.people: Fixed walking-stick housing
visitorStoryRoute.story: Walking sticks remain in their dedicated vitrines, with their saint connections retained.
